output.name: Skarún — The Hawk Over the Nets
output.myth: Ennu sat up all winter with sailcloth and cod-bone and made a hawk to frighten the gulls off the drying racks. Its wings were wide enough to shade a boat, and its belly held stones so it would keep its place. The gulls went shrieking to Tavo, who laughed and lifted the hawk by one wingtip. It went up past the Spindle and hung over the Reach, wings out, and has never come down. Orrun's breath rises from the Whale's Blow to the east, and the spray climbs up and wets the hawk's wings. The Turning Gulls keep watch on the north cliff, where the wind comes first, but Mesket never looks at the sea, so she has never seen it. My grandmother's mother said you can see it on still nights, low in the north, when the gulls are quiet. Ennu told it to wait until the gulls learned manners. The gulls have not learned manners. So the hawk keeps its wings out over nets that are gone. Mend your own net, child, and keep one eye up.
output.finding: Find the Turning Gulls standing watch in the north, then go one hand-span (about 20°) due south of them to find the Hawk Over the Nets, hanging wings-out in the Windward.
